newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Fourth private bank launched in Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: Fourth private bank launched in Ethiopia.

text.p: The National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE) on Thursday announced the launch of a fourth commercial bank, Wegagen, which has a subscribed capital of 60 million birr ($9.1 million).
NBE said in an announcement in the English language daily The Ethiopian Herald that half of the total par value of the shares, 30 million birr, was fully paid up in cash.

NBE said the biggest shareholder in Wegagen was Endowement Fund for the Rehabilitation of Tigray, a regional Ethiopian development group, with a paid up capital of 4.8 million birr ($726,832) and subscribed capital of 9.6 million birr.

Other shareholders include The Amhara National Regional Rehabilitation Development Organisation and Dinsho Private Limited Company -- who have paid up and subscribed capital of 4.5 million birr and 9.0 million birr respectively each.

Three private banks with aggregate authorised capital of 150 million birr have been licensed in Ethiopia since the government liberalised its financial system in 1994. They include the Awash Bank, Dashen Bank and Bank of Abyssinia.
The banks are fully owned by Ethiopians because the government does not yet allow foreigners to buy shares in private commercial banks. ($1=6.6 Ethiopian birr).
